target_customer: Originally mass-affluent consumers wanting a rewards debit card (as Point); now high-net-worth members paying about $1,000 to $3,000 per year for a charge card and concierge
problem: Debit card users earn no rewards while credit card rewards require debt. Later, affluent travelers wanted dining, hotel and event access bundled with a card.
business_model: Interchange plus annual membership fees; later a premium invite-only membership charge card with concierge
product_category: Fintech, rewards debit card then premium charge card

founders.name: Patrick Mrozowski
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him co-founder of Atlas (fka Point); Forbes Chile says he founded Point.

founders.name: Kenan Pulak
previous_startups: Two earlier startups in social and CRM (outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: first engineer at Motiv and Metal Pay, first mobile engineer at The RealReal.

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing on a bank-partner stack with rewards logic is standard fintech engineering, with compliance and partner dependence as hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Rewards debit depended on sponsor banks and interchange; Forbes Japan reports the bank partner Column ended the relationship, showing weak control.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied Point; the company stalled and pivoted to a premium charge card in 2023.

market_need_then: Consumers wanted card-style rewards without credit; Point's 2019 Product Hunt and Stanford Daily coverage show early interest, but the sources found do not quantify demand.

identity.visual_style: Premium charge card; members pick a personalized icon, no card number printed (NerdWallet)
identity.voice_and_tone: Luxury positioning: Your key to the world

branding.brand_signature: Your key to the world (tagline); invite-only waitlist card

rebrands.why: Pivot from rewards debit to a premium charge card after the bank partnership ended and spending concentrated in few customers (Forbes sources)

branding.community_and_virality: Fortune (2024-07) reported over 30,000 people on the waitlist; Doctor of Credit and a FICO forum discuss the card.

brand_strength.rationale: Fortune waitlist coverage and card-community discussion show pull for Atlas, but the earlier generic name Point did not stand out, and the name Atlas is shared with other firms.

pivots.to: Atlas, an invite-only charge card with concierge
pivots.why: Point burned cash with little revenue and was named a zombie fintech; 90 percent of spend came from 15 percent of customers (Forbes Japan via search summary)

outcome_analysis: Point raised a $10.5M Series A in 2020 and a $46.5M Series B in 2021 for a rewards debit card, then stalled: Forbes reports heavy spending, weak revenue and the loss of its bank partner, and it appeared doomed by April 2022. It renamed itself Atlas in 2023, focused on high-value members, reached a waitlist of 30,000 by July 2024 and raised a further $27M in December 2024. Whether the pivot is a durable success is not yet clear.
notes: Atlas (atlas-3) is fka Point per the YC page, which lists founded 2022 (wrong); Point was founded 2018 per Finextra and 2019 per other sources. Series A date is July 2020 per FinTech Futures; another source says March 2020. Total after Series B was about $60M per press. The 2024 round is labeled Series B-II by CB Insights; amount from FinSMEs and CB, investors not stated in sources opened (CB mentions Eric Schmidt). An aggregator lists a $40M Series C in April 2026, unverified. FinSMEs page could not be fetched (rate limit), so that round rests on search snippets plus a PR Newswire headline. Competition list left empty: sources found naming rivals (Chime) were dated 2020 or later, beyond a few months after the batch. Founder roles beyond Kenan Pulak come from the YC page only; Forbes figures come from search summaries.
